data_description.pool_type: Pre-selects the equipment modules. You can adjust them in the next step.

modules.title: Equipment modules
modules.description: Each enabled module creates its own entities and shows its own tiles on the maintenance page.

data_description.notify_service: For example notify.mobile_app_myphone. Leave empty for no built-in notifications — the "due" binary sensors and the maintenance event stay available for your own automations.

error.invalid_notify_service: Enter a service like notify.mobile_app_myphone, or leave it empty.

pool.title: Pool
pool.description: The volume unlocks the salt-dose hint. The salt band is what the readings are judged against — check what your chlorinator asks for.

data_description.maintenance_mode_enabled: Adds a switch that says somebody is working on the pool. On the maintenance page it comes with a sheet: what each piece of equipment should do while the work lasts, and for how long. When the time is up the visit ends and the equipment goes back to how it was found. Only the entities you assigned under Equipment are ever touched — and anyone holding the page link can start a visit.

modules.title: Equipment modules
modules.description: Entities and page tiles of disabled modules are removed.

people.title: People on the page
people.description: Choose which Home Assistant users appear as chips on the maintenance page. The generic Technician chip is always shown. Selecting everyone (or no one) shows all active users.

sensors.title: Linked sensors
sensors.description: Link existing sensors (e.g. from a smart probe or another pool integration) to this pool. Their current values are shown on the maintenance page next to the manual readings, and a snapshot is stored with every record. Leave a field empty to unlink it. With a pressure sensor linked, the filter wash alert follows the pressure rise over the clean baseline instead of the fixed interval. The baseline is captured automatically the next time a filter wash is logged.

data.report_sensors: Extra entities on the Status tab

equipment.title: Equipment
equipment.description: Point the dashboards at the entities that play a known role, instead of having them guess from the extra entity list.

data_description.filtration_schedule_mode: How this pool holds its filtration hours. A schedule helper is Home Assistant's own; pick the entities instead when the pool controller already publishes the on and off times.

schedule_helper.title: Filtration schedule
schedule_helper.description: The schedule helper that decides when the filtration runs. Its weekly blocks are shown on every dashboard, and today's hours with them.

schedule_times.title: Filtration schedule
schedule_times.description: The entities your pool controller uses for its cycle. The two times build the same weekly view a schedule helper would, and the sensor says whether the filtration is running right now.

data_description.filtration_state_entity: Leave empty to read the state off the hours themselves.

data.filter_pressure_rise: Wash the filter at this pressure rise (%)

page.title: Page and notifications

data_description.notify_service: For example notify.mobile_app_myphone. Leave empty for no built-in notifications — the "due" binary sensors and the maintenance event stay available for your own automations.
data_description.report_enabled: Adds a read-only report tab to the public page: current values, task status and recent records. Anyone with the page URL can see it.
data_description.kiosk_enabled: A dark, display-only dashboard for a screen next to the pool (7" landscape and up): water readings, equipment and a countdown to the next schedule change. No touch or navigation. Find its URL in the QR code entity's attributes.

page.description: Pick a notify service (like your phone from the companion app) or a notify entity. Leave it empty and the integration sends nothing — the *due* binary sensors and the maintenance event are still there for your own automations.

security.title: Security
security.description: Regenerating the access token invalidates the current page URL. You will need to rewrite your QR code or NFC tag.

error.invalid_notify_service: Enter a service like notify.mobile_app_myphone, or leave it empty.

options.water_chemistry: Extended water chemistry (CYA, hardness, total chlorine)

options.manual_only: Show on page only (entities stay manual)
options.fill_on_record: Fill entities from probe when a record is saved
options.mirror: Mirror linked sensors continuously (overrides manual values)

options.times: On time, off time and a running sensor

delete_record.name: Delete record
delete_record.description: Deletes a maintenance record (the most recent one when no id is given) and rebuilds the task timestamps from the remaining records.

config_entry.name: Pool
config_entry.description: The pool to delete the record from.

record_id.name: Record id
record_id.description: Id of the record to delete (see the recent_records attribute of the last-record sensor). Leave empty to delete the most recent record.

start_maintenance.name: Start maintenance
start_maintenance.description: Raises the maintenance flag with a window and an equipment plan, the way the maintenance page does. Turn it off again with switch.turn_off, which also puts the equipment back.

config_entry.name: Pool
config_entry.description: The pool to start maintenance on.

minutes.name: For how long
minutes.description: Minutes until the visit ends by itself and the equipment goes back to how it was. Leave empty for no limit.

equipment.name: Equipment
equipment.description: What each equipment role should do while the visit lasts — for example pool_system: off and heat_pump: on. Covers take open or closed. Roles you leave out are not touched.
